dn32:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Rājagaha on the Vultures’ Peak mountain.
dn32:1.3: Then the Four Great Kings, with a great army of yakkhas, with a great army of gandhabbas, with a great army of kumbhaṇḍas, with a great army of nāgas, having set up a protection over the four quarters, having set serried troops at the four directions, having set up a barricade at the four directions, at the end of the night, having lit up the whole of Vultures’ Peak with their surpassing beauty, approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, they sat down on one side.
dn32:1.4: Then of those yakkhas, some, after worshipping the Fortunate One, sat down on one side. Some exchanged greetings with the Fortunate One, and after exchanging polite and courteous greetings, sat down on one side. Some, after raising their hands in respectful salutation to the Fortunate One, sat down on one side. Some, after announcing their name and family, sat down on one side. Some, while keeping silent, sat down on one side.

dn32:2.2: “There are, reverend Sir, some high ranking yakkhas who are not pleased with the Fortunate One,

dn32:2.8: But, reverend Sir, almost all of the yakkhas are not pleased with the Fortunate One.
dn32:2.9: What is the reason for that?
dn32:2.10: Because, reverend Sir, the Fortunate One preaches the Dhamma of refraining from killing living creatures, preaches the Dhamma of refraining from taking what has not been given, preaches the Dhamma of refraining from sexual misconduct, preaches the Dhamma of refraining from false speech, preaches the Dhamma of refraining from liquor, wines, or intoxicants which cause heedlessness.
dn32:2.11: But, reverend Sir, almost all of the yakkhas do not refrain from killing living creatures, do not refrain from taking what has not been given, do not refrain from sexual misconduct, do not refrain from false speech, do not refrain from liquors, wines, or intoxicants which cause heedlessness.
dn32:2.12: To them that is neither dear nor appealing.
dn32:2.13: There are, reverend Sir, disciples of the Fortunate One in the wilderness, who are practising in remote jungle dwelling places, where there is little sound, little noise, which have a lonely atmosphere, lying hidden away from men, which are suitable for seclusion.
dn32:2.14: And there are high ranking yakkhas settled there who are not pleased with the word of the Fortunate One,
dn32:2.15: To please then, reverend Sir, may the Fortunate One learn this “Āṭānāṭiya” protection, for the monks’, nuns’, laymen’s, and laywomen’s guard, protection, freedom from harm, and comfortable living.”

dn32:8.1: This, dear Sir, is the “Āṭānāṭiya” protection, for the monks’, nuns’, laymen’s, and laywomen’s guard, protection, freedom from harm, and comfortable living.
dn32:8.2: Whoever, dear Sir - be they monk or nun or layman or laywoman - learns this “Āṭānāṭiya” protection well, and will master it in its entirety,
dn32:8.3: then if a non-human being - be they male yakkha or female yakkha or yakkha boy or yakkha girl or yakkha minister or yakkha councillor or yakkha messenger or male gandhabba or female gandhabba or gandhabba boy or gandhabba girl or gandhabba minister or gandhabba councillor or gandhabba messenger or male kumbhaṇḍa or female kumbhaṇḍa or kumbhaṇḍa boy or kumbhaṇḍa girl or kumbhaṇḍa minister or kumbhaṇḍa councillor or kumbhaṇḍa messenger or male nāga or female nāga or nāga boy or nāga girl or nāga minister or nāga councillor or nāga messenger - with a wicked mind come near while they are going, or stand near while they are standing, or sit near while they are sitting, or lie near while they are lying,
dn32:8.4: then that non-human being, dear Sir, would not receive in my villages and towns, honour or respect.
dn32:8.5: That non-human being, dear Sir, would not receive in my royal city Ālakamandā, ground or dwelling.
dn32:8.6: That non-human being, dear Sir, would not be able to go to the gathering of the yakkhas.
dn32:8.7: Further, dear Sir, non-human beings would not give or take him in marriage.
dn32:8.8: Further, dear Sir, non-human beings would abuse him with very personal abuse.
dn32:8.9: Further, dear Sir, non-human beings would drop an empty bowl over his head.
dn32:8.10: Further, dear Sir, non-human beings would split his head into seven pieces.
dn32:9.1: There are non-human beings, dear Sir, who are fierce, cruel, and violent, they do not take notice of the Great Kings, they do not take notice of the Great Kings’ men, they do not take notice of the Great Kings’ mens’ men,
dn32:9.2: and those non-human beings, dear Sir, are said to be in revolt against the Great Kings.
dn32:9.3: Just as, dear Sir, there are thieves in the king of Magadha’s realm,
dn32:9.4: who do not take notice of the king of Magadha, who do not take notice of the king of Magadha’s men, who do not take notice of the king of Magadha’s mens’ men,
dn32:9.5: and those great thieves, dear Sir, are said to be in revolt against the king of Magadha.
dn32:9.6: Even so, dear Sir, there are non-human beings who are fierce, cruel, and violent, they do not take notice of the Great Kings, they do not take notice of the Great Kings’ men, they do not take notice of the Great Kings’ mens’ men,
dn32:9.7: and those non-human beings, dear Sir, are said to be in revolt against the Great Kings.
dn32:9.8: Now, dear Sir, whatever non-human beings - be they male yakkha or female yakkha or yakkha boy or yakkha girl or yakkha minister or yakkha councillor or yakkha messenger or male gandhabba or female gandhabba or gandhabba boy or gandhabba girl or gandhabba minister or gandhabba councillor or gandhabba messenger or male kumbhaṇḍa or female kumbhaṇḍa or kumbhaṇḍa boy or kumbhaṇḍa girl or kumbhaṇḍa minister or kumbhaṇḍa councillor or kumbhaṇḍa messenger or male nāga or female nāga or nāga boy or nāga girl or nāga minister or nāga councillor or nāga messenger - with a wicked mind should come near a monk or a nun or a layman or a laywoman while they are going, or stand near while they are standing, or sit near while they are sitting, or lie near while they are lying,

dn32:12.270: “This yakkha has seized me, this yakkha has grabbed me, this yakkha annoys me, this yakkha harasses me, this yakkha hurts me, this yakkha injures me, this yakkha will not release me.”
dn32:12.271: This, dear Sir, is the “Āṭānāṭiyā” protection, for the monks’, nuns’, laymen’s, and laywomen’s guard, protection, freedom from harm, and comfortable living.
dn32:12.272: And now, dear Sir, we shall go, as we have many duties, and there is much which ought to be done.”
dn32:12.273: “Now is the time for whatever you Great Kings are thinking.”
dn32:12.274: Then the Four Great Kings, monks, rose from their seats and after worshipping and circumambulating me, vanished right there.
dn32:12.275: Then some yakkhas, monks, rose from their seats and after worshipping and circumambulating me, vanished right there.
dn32:12.276: Some exchanged greetings with me, and after exchanging polite and courteous greetings, vanished right there.
dn32:12.277: Some, after raising their hands in respectful salutation to me, vanished right there.
dn32:12.278: Some, after announcing their name and family vanished right there.
dn32:12.279: And some, while keeping silent, vanished right there.
dn32:13.3: bear in mind the “Āṭānāṭiya” protection, monks,
dn32:13.4: the “Āṭānāṭiya” protection, monks, is for your welfare and benefit, for the monks’, nuns’, laymen’s, and laywomen’s guard, protection, freedom from harm, and comfortable living.”
dn32:13.6: and those monks were uplifted and greatly rejoiced in what was said by the Fortunate One.
